title: What If Saturn Lost Its Rings? It's Already Happening

scenes.text: What if Saturn lost its rings? It's already happening, and the clock is running.
Ice from the rings keeps falling into Saturn as ring rain, an estimated 420 to 2,800 kilograms every second.
Researchers say that's enough water to fill an Olympic swimming pool in about half an hour.
Add the ring material Cassini saw falling into Saturn's equator, and the rings could be gone in under 100 million years.
Ring rain alone would take about 300 million years. Either way, the rings are not permanent.
Saturn would look like any other gas giant. Some scientists think we're seeing the rings in the middle of their lifetime.
